Between I-5 and Eastgate Mall, the southbound bike lane areas are uneven and have vertical ruts that can catch a bicycle wheel and cause a crash. LEMON GROVE (KGTV) ? A Lemon Grove mother got broken ribs and chipped teeth after a violent bike crash along 69th Street.

Rosie Vazquez says she was riding her bike down a hill near Dartmoor Drive on May 21 when she hit a pothole and flipped her bike.

She says it happened as cars began passing her.

?A car passed and another car passed, as I looked back to clear my path I didn?t anticipate bumping into this pothole,? Vazquez said.

There were a few potholes on the street, so she wasn?t sure which one hit her bike. Nearly a month later, she says her medical bills are adding up and thinks she needs to be compensated.

?Pain and suffering, damage to myself, time off from work,? she said listing all the reasons why she hired an attorney.

Her Attorney, Evan Walker, says this is not the first time someone has gotten hurt from a pothole. Many have come to him with similar stories, asking to help them file a claim.

?I would think that would be proper for the city to upgrade its infrastructure instead of paying out,? Walker said.

The thing is, it?s not immediately clear which city maintains the road - because 69th Street falls right on the city lines of San Diego and Lemon Grove.

Lemon Grove?s Assistant City Manager and Public Works Director responded to 10News via email. The statement reads in part:

?69th Street is a street that is located between the City of San Diego and the City of Lemon Grove.  The City has, in the past, maintained portions of 69th Street. 

However, without being able to access the City?s past project information at this time, I cannot speak to this actual location and if the City of Lemon Grove has treated it. ?

10News also reached out to the city of San Diego, asking whether there is a joint effort in maintaining 69th Street. A spokeswoman said ?it is possible? but they would have to check with an engineer for more details.

Walker plans to file a claim with both cities next week.

?It shouldn?t be like this,? Vazquez said, referring to the condition of the road.

public_description:
The picture labeled "Storm Drain" is the source of the water from 5952 La Jolla Scenic.  A worker from Water Utilities told me that this is not a drain in that water is meant to come out, not go in.  He claimed the water is from an overflowing fountain on the adjacent property. "Eastbound Curb" shows the water running east on LJ Scenic towards the intersection with Rutgers.

"Looking East" shows the intersection of La Jolla Scenic (north is to the right) and Rutgers. La Jolla Scenic has a 90 degree turn at this point so all the visible street is La Jolla Scenic.  Note that the water actually appears to start in the middle of the intersection.  Sometimes it goes all the way across and sometimes it starts in the middle even though the source is on the far (west) side.  My guess is that the water goes underground on the west side and comes up again in the middle before heading the rest of the way across and down Rutgers.  It is probably eroding the ground under the intersection.  Sinkhole here we come!

"Rutgers Stop Sign" has Rutgers on the right and La Jolla Scenic heading north towards the cross on the left.  If you look closely, you can see the water running down the Rutgers curb.  "Intersection" shows the same intersection from the opposite (north west) corner. As I mentioned previously, there is also a constant flow of water coming down the west curb of La Jolla Scenic visible in "Rutgers Stop Sign" from beyond where the two cars are parked.  That water is coming from the back of a house on La Jolla Rancho.  I did not get any decent pictures of that problem.  However, if you look at "Intersection" you can see there is a significant amount of water uphill from the low point.  All that water is coming from the La Jolla Rancho house.

"Potholes" shows just some of the potholes at the intersection.  A single 2 dimensional photo cannot do justice to the problem.

Situation:  On Main Street just south of 32nd street there was a repair of a trench.  The truck belonged to Kay Construction Company. There were warnings of a closed lane but NO warning of an open trench. The trench was about 20 inches wide and at least 2 inches deep.  Without a bike lane we were using the narrow traffic lane and moving at about 8 to 10 miles per hour in to avoid being hit from the rear by cars or trucks.  Even after seeing the trench, I was unable to slow to avoid striking the trench at a safe speed.  Without specific warning my bike wheels struck edge of the trench with such force that I lost my balance.  The jolt from striking the trench was so severe that my water bottle was ejected from its cage and shattered on the street.  Several of the other bike riders in our small group had ruptured innertubes and punched tires.  As I was taking phone photos of the scene, the man from the company who appeared to be in charge seemed indifferent to the danger.  He blamed us stating that warning was adequate.  There was no flagman to warn us or other vehicle drivers of this hazard. It appeared to me that at least one of the construction company staff who holding a slow signs was distracted by his cell phones.  I got a phone number from https://kayconstructionco.com/.  I called (619) 654-9075 and gave my name when asked and said I had a bike accident on Main Street.  He said, ?I was on-site?.  I asked for a mailing address. ?I will not give you an address?  he then hung up.  I called again and there was no answer.   Thank you for your attention to this matter.
